title: Disconnected entities: Update and Attach
summary: Saving objects that came from outside the context, like a web request body.

steps.title: When the context did not load it
body: In a web API, the object you save often did not come from a query. A client sends JSON, and ASP.NET Core turns it into a **new** `Item` object. A fresh context (one per request) has never seen it: it is **detached**. You must tell the context what it is.
**`db.Update(item)`** says "this exists; save **all** its values". The entity becomes `Modified` with every property marked changed:
```sql
UPDATE "Items" SET "Name" = @p0, "PriceCents" = @p1, "Stock" = @p2 WHERE "Id" = @p3
**`db.Attach(item)`** says "this exists and is **unchanged**". Nothing is saved until you change something *after* attaching; then only those properties are sent:
```csharp
var item = new Item { Id = 3 };      // just the key
db.Attach(item);
item.Stock = 0;                       // now only Stock is Modified
db.SaveChanges();                     // UPDATE "Items" SET "Stock" = @p0 WHERE "Id" = @p1
(An entity with no key value set, like `Id = 0`, is treated as new: `Update` and `Attach` mark it `Added`.)

code: seed.Items.AddRange(new Item { Name = "pen", Stock = 10, PriceCents = 150 }, new Item { Name = "ink", Stock = 0, PriceCents = 400 },
var fromClient = new Item { Id = 1, Name = "pen", Stock = 4, PriceCents = 150 };
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=shop.db");
steps.explain: `Update` marks every non-key property modified (Name, Stock, PriceCents). `Attach` starts `Unchanged`; only the property changed afterwards is sent. The stub's `Name` was empty, but because it was never marked modified, the stored name `pad` is kept.

steps.prompt: A client sends `{ "id": 3, "stock": 7 }` with no name or price. Your code deserialises it into an `Item` and calls `db.Update(item); db.SaveChanges();`. What happens?
options: The row's Name and PriceCents are overwritten with an empty string and 0
Nothing: Update needs a loaded entity
EF Core throws because Name is missing
steps.explain: `Update` sends **every** property. The missing ones are just their C# defaults on the object, and those overwrite the stored values. For partial updates, load the entity (or attach a stub) and set only what the client sent.

steps.title: The safe pattern for an edit
body: For an API's `PUT /items/{id}` the clearest and safest pattern is: **load, copy, save.**
```csharp
var item = db.Items.Find(id);
if (item is null) return Results.NotFound();
item.Name = dto.Name;
item.PriceCents = dto.PriceCents;      // only the fields this endpoint may change
db.SaveChanges();                      // UPDATE of the columns that really changed
It costs one `SELECT`, and in return:
- a missing row is a clean 404, not an exception,
- fields the client must not change (like `Stock`, or an owner id) cannot be overwritten by a malicious body,
- unchanged values are not written at all.
`Update` and `Attach` shine when you **trust** the whole object (it came from your own code), or when saving that `SELECT` really matters.

items: A PUT endpoint that may change only Name and Price
An edit form where some fields are read-only
Saving a complete object your own code built and keeps in a cache
Marking item 42 as discontinued without reading it first
Bumping the view count of a known post id
steps.explain: Load-copy-save is the default for input from outside. `Update` writes everything, so only use it for objects you trust completely. A stub plus `Attach` updates one column with no `SELECT`.

steps.prompt: Arrange a PATCH that sets only the price of item `id`, without loading it first.
lines: var stub = new Item { Id = id };
steps.explain: Attach first, so the context records the stub as `Unchanged`; then the change to `PriceCents` is detected as the only modification. Setting the price before attaching would not mark it modified.

code: seed.Items.AddRange(new Item { Name = "pen", Stock = 10, PriceCents = 150 }, new Item { Name = "ink", Stock = 0, PriceCents = 400 },
var stub = new Item { Id = 2, PriceCents = 999 };
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=shop.db");
steps.explain: The price was set **before** `Attach`, so it is part of what the context believes is the unchanged, stored state. Nothing is modified, nothing is saved: the order of those lines matters.

steps.title: A safe edit
prompt: The tests give you `ShopDb` with `Items` (`Id`, `Name`, `Stock`, `PriceCents`), and this request type:
record ItemEdit(int Id, string Name, int PriceCents, int Stock);
- `bool Edit(ShopDb db, ItemEdit edit)`: the **load, copy, save** pattern. Copy only `Name` and `PriceCents` (stock is managed elsewhere and must be ignored). Return `false` for an unknown id.
- `void Discontinue(ShopDb db, int id)`: set `Stock` to 0 for that item **without loading it**: attach a stub, change `Stock`, save. Only the `Stock` column may be written.
solution: var stub = new Item { Id = id, Stock = -1 };
template: seed.Items.AddRange(new Item { Name = "pen", Stock = 10, PriceCents = 150 }, new Item { Name = "ink", Stock = 0, PriceCents = 400 },
Dojo.Eq("Edit(1) returns true", true, Edit(dojoDb, new ItemEdit(1, "fountain pen", 900, 9999)));
Dojo.Eq("Edit(42) returns false", false, Edit(dojoDb, new ItemEdit(42, "x", 1, 1)));
Dojo.Eq("name and price were copied", "fountain pen 900", dojoPen.Name + " " + dojoPen.PriceCents);

Dojo.Check("...an UPDATE of Stock only, without a SELECT", dojoSql.Count == 1 && dojoSql[0].StartsWith("UPDATE") && dojoSql[0].Contains("\"Stock\"") && !dojoSql[0].Contains("\"Name\"") && !dojoSql[0].Contains("PriceCents"), string.Join(" | ", dojoSql));
Dojo.Eq("pad is discontinued but keeps its name", "pad 0", dojoDb.Items.Where(i => i.Id == 3).Select(i => i.Name + " " + i.Stock).Single());
record ItemEdit(int Id, string Name, int PriceCents, int Stock);
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=shop.db")
hints: For the stub, the value of `Stock` before `Attach` must differ from 0, or setting it to 0 is not a change: `new Item { Id = id, Stock = -1 }`.
